# About this qmd {.unnumbered}

Builds the main PUMA-level dataset: one row per 2020 PUMA (2,462,
covering the 50 states and DC) with the outcomes and controls for
2022–2024. Prison exposure is built separately in
`processing_prison_exposure.qmd` and joined on in the analysis qmd.

Controls and divorce come from the 2022, 2023 and 2024 ACS 1-year
samples pooled together.

The period overdose rate is total deaths over total person-years, summed
over all tracts in the PUMA and all three years (not an average of
rates):

$$Rate_{p,2022\text{–}2024} = 100{,}000 \times \frac{\sum_{y}\sum_{t \in p} D_{ty}}{\sum_{y}\sum_{t \in p} N_{t}}$$

$D_{ty}$ is the CDC death count where it's reported. Counts between 1
and 9 (and a few higher ranges) are suppressed, but the rate is still
given, so for those the count is estimated as rate × population and kept
inside the reported range. $N_t$ is the tract's 2020 census population.

Outputs, all in `data/final/`:

-   `national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.csv` and
    `rural_puma_dataset_2022_2024.csv`
-   `national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg`: the national table with PUMA
    boundaries, for maps and spatial models
-   `tract_overdose_by_year_2022_2024.csv` and
    `tract_overdose_2022_2024.csv`: tract-level outcome, for a
    tract-level check later

When reading the CSVs back, read the IDs as text so the leading zeros
survive:
`read_csv(file, col_types = cols(GEOID20 = col_character(), state_fips = col_character()))`.

Units: shares are percentages (0–100). Exceptions are death rates (per
100,000), median income (2024 dollars), land area (km²), density (people
per km²), counts and logs.

# Setup {#sec-setup}

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)  
library(sf)          
library(tidycensus)  
library(tigris)      
library(ipumsr)      

options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)  

# range of years used
years <- 2022:2024  

# 2-digit codes for the 50 states + DC
state_fips <- tidycensus::fips_codes %>%
  distinct(state_code) %>%
  filter(as.numeric(state_code) <= 56) %>%
  pull(state_code)
```

# Building the dataset {#sec-build}

### Codes and the institutional population

People in institutions (prisons, nursing homes, etc.) are dropped so
prisoners don't shift a PUMA's race, education and poverty figures.

```{r}
#| label: ipums-codes
#confirm the variable codes
ipums_val_labels(ddi, GQTYPE)    # 1-4 = institutions (prisons, nursing homes, etc.)
ipums_val_labels(ddi, MARST)     # 1-3 = married/separated, 4 = divorced
ipums_val_labels(ddi, DIVINYR)   # 1 = No, 2 = Yes, 0/8 = outside universe / suppressed
ipums_val_labels(ddi, EMPSTAT)   # 1 = employed, 2 = unemployed, 3 = not in labor force
ipums_val_labels(ddi, EDUC)      # 10 = 4 years of college, 11 = 5+ years
ipums_val_labels(ddi, RACE)      # 1 = White
ipums_val_labels(ddi, HISPAN)    # 0 = Not Hispanic, 9 = Not reported

#remove everyone living in an institution (prisons, nursing homes, etc.).
data_noninst <- data_ipums %>%
  filter(!GQTYPE %in% c(1, 2, 3, 4)) %>%
  #creates puma_geoid (state code + puma)
  mutate(puma_geoid = paste0(sprintf("%02d", STATEFIP), sprintf("%05d", PUMA))) 
```

### PUMA-level variables

Percentages are ratios of weighted counts, so pooling three years
doesn't need any adjustment. Weights for each year add up to that year's
population, so `total_pop` is divided by 3 to get an average year.
Incomes are converted to 2024 dollars with `CPI99` before taking the
median.

```{r}
#| label: ipums-puma
n_years <- n_distinct(data_noninst$YEAR)   # 3

# Person-level variables
# sum(PERWT * (condition)) adds up the weights of the people for whom the condition is TRUE
puma_person <- data_noninst %>%
  group_by(puma_geoid) %>%
  summarise(
    # Population (non-institutionalized), average over 2022-2024
    total_pop = sum(PERWT) / n_years,

    # Race: % whose race is not White (Hispanic Whites count as White)
    pct_nonwhite    = 100 * (1 - sum(PERWT * (RACE == 1)) / sum(PERWT)),
    # Alternative: % who are not non-Hispanic White (excludes HISPAN "not reported")
    pct_nonwhite_nh = 100 * (1 - sum(PERWT * (RACE == 1 & HISPAN == 0)) / sum(PERWT * (HISPAN != 9))),

    # Age structure: % aged 25-54, the ages with the highest overdose mortality
    pct_age_25_54 = 100 * sum(PERWT * between(AGE, 25, 54)) / sum(PERWT),

    # Education: % of people 25+ with a bachelor's degree or more
    pct_bachelors_plus = 100 * sum(PERWT * (EDUC >= 10 & AGE >= 25)) / sum(PERWT * (AGE >= 25)),

    # Poverty: % below the poverty line, among people with a poverty status (POVERTY = 0 is N/A)
    pct_poverty = 100 * sum(PERWT * (POVERTY > 0 & POVERTY < 100)) / sum(PERWT * (POVERTY > 0)),

    # Unemployment: % of the labor force (employed + unemployed) that is unemployed
    pct_unemployed = 100 * sum(PERWT * (EMPSTAT == 2)) / sum(PERWT * (EMPSTAT %in% c(1, 2))),

    # Divorce outcomes 
    # Main outcome: % of ever-married people (15+) who divorced in the past 12 months
    pct_divorced_past_yr = 100 * sum(PERWT * (DIVINYR == 2)) / sum(PERWT * (DIVINYR %in% c(1, 2))),

    # Unweighted sample sizes over all three years, to judge reliability
    n_person_sample   = n(),
    n_divorced_sample = sum(DIVINYR == 2)
  )

# Annual divorce rates, to check whether one year drives the result
puma_divorce_annual <- data_noninst %>%
  group_by(puma_geoid, YEAR) %>%
  summarise(pct_div = 100 * sum(PERWT * (DIVINYR == 2)) / sum(PERWT * (DIVINYR %in% c(1, 2))),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = YEAR, values_from = pct_div, names_prefix = "pct_divorced_past_yr_")

# Median household income in 2024 dollars
# One record per household (PERNUM == 1) with the household weight; HHINCOME = 9999999 is N/A.
# HHINCOME * CPI99 gives 1999 dollars; dividing by the 2024 CPI99 value gives 2024 dollars.
cpi99_2024 <- data_noninst %>%
  filter(YEAR == 2024) %>%
  distinct(CPI99) %>%
  pull(CPI99)
cpi99_2024   # should be a single number

# Weighted median: sort households by income, add up their weights, and take the
# first income where the running total reaches half of the PUMA's total weight.
puma_household <- data_noninst %>%
  filter(PERNUM == 1, HHINCOME != 9999999) %>%
  mutate(hhincome_2024 = HHINCOME * CPI99 / cpi99_2024) %>%
  group_by(puma_geoid) %>%
  arrange(hhincome_2024, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(n_hh_sample = n(),
         cum_share   = cumsum(HHWT) / sum(HHWT)) %>%
  filter(cum_share >= 0.5) %>%
  slice_head(n = 1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(puma_geoid, medhhinc = hhincome_2024, n_hh_sample)

# Combine and add logs
puma_summary <- puma_person %>%
  left_join(puma_divorce_annual, by = "puma_geoid") %>%
  left_join(puma_household, by = "puma_geoid") %>%
  mutate(
    log_pop      = log(total_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc)
  )

nrow(puma_summary)                        # should be 2462
```

## PUMA boundaries

```{r}
#| label: puma-geography
# Cartographic-boundary PUMA polygons for the 50 states + DC
pumas_2020 <- pumas(cb = TRUE, year = 2020) %>%
  filter(STATEFP20 %in% state_fips)   # 50 states + DC (drops Puerto Rico and Guam)

# Start the master PUMA dataset: boundaries + IPUMS variables
puma_final <- pumas_2020 %>%
  left_join(puma_summary, by = c("GEOID20" = "puma_geoid"))

nrow(puma_final)                    # should be 2462
sum(is.na(puma_final$total_pop))    # PUMAs with no IPUMS match 
```

## Tract populations and crosswalks

`tract_pop_2020` gives the tract populations used as denominators and
weights (downloaded the first time, then read from the saved file).
`rel20` assigns tracts to PUMAs. The RUCA file also has a crosswalk from
Connecticut's post-2022 tract IDs to the 2020 IDs used everywhere else,
which is needed for the CDC data.

```{r}
#| label: tract-pop-download
#| eval: false
# one-time download of 2020 census tract populations (needs a Census API key).
#get_decennial(
#  geography = "tract",
#  state     = state_fips,          # all 50 states + DC in one call
#  year      = 2020,
#  sumfile   = "pl",
#  variables = c(tot_pop          = "P1_001N",   # total population
#                pop_inst_gq      = "P5_002N",   # people in institutional group quarters
#                pop_correctional = "P5_003N"),  # people in adult correctional facilities
#  output    = "wide"
#) %>%
#  select(GEOID, tot_pop, pop_inst_gq, pop_correctional) %>%
#  write_csv("data/raw/tract_pop_2020.csv")
```

```{r}
#| label: tract-pop-load
# 2020 census tract populations. GEOID is read as text so the leading zeros survive
tract_pop_2020 <- read_csv("data/raw/tract_pop_2020.csv",
                           col_types = cols(GEOID = col_character()))
```

```{r}
#| label: tract-crosswalks
# Census tract -> 2020 PUMA relationship file.
# rel20: GEOID = 11-digit tract ID, GEOID20 = 7-digit PUMA ID.
rel20 <- read_csv("https://www2.census.gov/geo/docs/maps-data/data/rel2020/2020_Census_Tract_to_2020_PUMA.txt",
                  col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  transmute(
    GEOID   = paste0(STATEFP, COUNTYFP, TRACTCE),
    GEOID20 = paste0(STATEFP, PUMA5CE)
  )

# RUCA file: also provides a translator from Connecticut's post-2022 tract IDs
# (planning regions, TractFIPS23) to the 2020 IDs (TractFIPS20) used everywhere else.
ruca_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/rurality/RUCA-codes-2020-tract.csv",
                     col_types = cols(.default = "c"))

xwalk <- ruca_raw %>%
  filter(!is.na(TractFIPS23)) %>%
  distinct(TractFIPS23, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(TractFIPS23, TractFIPS20)

# Total 2020 population of each PUMA (all tracts), used for the coverage measure below
puma_pop_2020 <- tract_pop_2020 %>%
  inner_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%   # keeps only tracts that have a PUMA
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(puma_pop_2020 = sum(tot_pop))
```

## Overdose deaths (CDC, 2022–2024)

```{r}
#| label: cdc-inspect
injury_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/injury_overdose_violence_census_tract.csv")

names(injury_raw)          # GEOID (tract group), NAME (its tracts), Count, Rate, ...
table(injury_raw$Period)   # 2022, 2023, 2024, and TTM (trailing twelve months; not used)
table(injury_raw$Intent)   # "Drug_OD" is the overdose category
```

### Deaths by tract and year

```{r}
#| label: cdc-tract-year
# One row per real tract per year, with an estimated number of overdose deaths.
#
# How the CDC file is organized:
# - Each row is a tract or a group of small tracts: GEOID = group ID, NAME = the group's
#   tracts. Count and Rate belong to the whole group.
# - Count is text. Exact counts are given for 0 and most larger numbers; otherwise it shows
#   a range ("1-9", "10-15", "16-20", "21-25", "=26" meaning 26 or more). The rate is
#   still reported for those rows.
#
# How deaths are built:
# 1. Exact count where there is one. For a range, estimate the count as
#    rate x group population / 100,000, kept within the reported range.
# 2. Split the group's deaths among its tracts in proportion to their 2020 population,
#    so adding tracts back up never double-counts.
od_tract_year <- injury_raw %>%
  filter(Intent == "Drug_OD", Period %in% years) %>%
  transmute(
    group_id  = GEOID,
    NAME,
    year      = as.integer(Period),
    count_raw = Count,
    rate      = na_if(as.numeric(Rate), -999)   # -999 = rate suppressed
  ) %>%
  # One row per real tract
  separate_rows(NAME, sep = ",\\s*") %>%
  mutate(GEOID = str_trim(NAME)) %>%
  select(-NAME) %>%
  # Translate Connecticut's new tract IDs to 2020 IDs (other states unchanged)
  left_join(xwalk, by = c("GEOID" = "TractFIPS23")) %>%
  mutate(GEOID = coalesce(TractFIPS20, GEOID)) %>%
  select(-TractFIPS20) %>%
  # Attach each tract's PUMA and 2020 population
  left_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(tract_pop_2020 %>% select(GEOID, tot_pop), by = "GEOID") %>%
  # Group-level deaths, then each tract's share
  group_by(group_id, year) %>%
  mutate(
    group_pop     = sum(tot_pop, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Exact count if Count is just a number, otherwise NA (it's a range)
    count_exact   = if_else(str_detect(count_raw, "^\\d+$"), parse_number(count_raw), NA_real_),
    count_imputed = is.na(count_exact),
    # Bounds of a range: "1-9" -> 1 and 9; "=26" (26 or more) -> 26 and no upper limit
    count_lo = parse_number(count_raw),
    count_hi = if_else(str_detect(count_raw, "^\\d+-\\d+$"),
                       parse_number(str_extract(count_raw, "\\d+$")), Inf),
    # Estimate from the rate
    count_est = rate * group_pop / 1e5,
    # Exact count if there is one; otherwise the estimate, kept within the range
    group_deaths = case_when(
      !count_imputed       ~ count_exact,
      count_est < count_lo ~ count_lo,
      count_est > count_hi ~ count_hi,
      TRUE                 ~ count_est
    ),
    deaths = group_deaths * tot_pop / group_pop
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Checks: matching
od_tract_year %>% count(GEOID, year) %>% filter(n > 1) %>% nrow()   # duplicates; should be 0

od_tract_year %>%
  summarise(matched_to_puma = mean(!is.na(GEOID20)),   # want ~1
            has_population  = mean(!is.na(tot_pop)),   # want ~1
            has_deaths      = mean(!is.na(deaths)))    # want ~1

od_tract_year %>%
  filter(str_starts(GEOID, "09")) %>%                  # Connecticut
  summarise(ct_matched_to_puma = mean(!is.na(GEOID20)))   # want ~1

# Checks: counts
# How many groups needed an estimated count, by year
od_tract_year %>%
  distinct(group_id, year, count_imputed) %>%
  count(year, count_imputed)

# Total deaths by year (should follow the national trend, with a large drop in 2024)
od_tract_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(total_deaths = sum(deaths, na.rm = TRUE))

# Are 2020 census populations close to the CDC's denominators?
# For groups with an exact count above zero, count / rate x 100,000 is the CDC's denominator.
od_tract_year %>%
  distinct(group_id, year, count_exact, rate, group_pop) %>%
  filter(count_exact > 0, rate > 0) %>%
  mutate(ratio = (count_exact / rate * 1e5) / group_pop) %>%
  pull(ratio) %>%
  summary()                                            # median near 1 = estimates sound

# How often the rate-based estimate fell outside the reported range (and was pulled back in)
od_tract_year %>%
  distinct(group_id, year, count_imputed, count_est, count_lo, count_hi) %>%
  filter(count_imputed) %>%
  summarise(share_below   = mean(count_est < count_lo, na.rm = TRUE),
            share_above   = mean(count_est > count_hi, na.rm = TRUE),
            share_no_rate = mean(is.na(count_est)))
```

```{r}
#| label: cdc-annual
od_puma_year <- od_tract_year %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(deaths), tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20, year) %>%
  summarise(deaths = sum(deaths), pop = sum(tot_pop), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(rate = 1e5 * deaths / pop)

# Wide version, kept in the dataset for the "is one year driving the result?" check
od_puma_annual <- od_puma_year %>%
  select(GEOID20, year, rate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = rate, names_prefix = "overdose_rate_")

# 1. Distributions by year
od_puma_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(rate), median = median(rate), sd = sd(rate), n_pumas = n())

ggplot(od_puma_year, aes(rate, colour = factor(year))) +
  geom_density() +
  labs(title = "PUMA overdose rates by year", x = "Deaths per 100,000", colour = "Year") +
  theme_minimal()

# 2. Year-to-year correlation of PUMA rates (and rank correlation, less sensitive to outliers)
od_puma_annual %>%
  select(starts_with("overdose_rate_")) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs")

od_puma_annual %>%
  select(starts_with("overdose_rate_")) %>%
  cor(use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman")

# 3. Maps by year (lower 48 shown; Alaska and Hawaii would stretch the map)
pumas_2020 %>%
  filter(!STATEFP20 %in% c("02", "15")) %>%
  select(GEOID20) %>%
  inner_join(od_puma_year, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = rate), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Per 100,000", option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 1) +
  theme_void()
```

### Pooled period rate

```{r}
#| label: cdc-pooled
# Number of years pooled (3)
n_years <- od_tract_year %>% distinct(year) %>% nrow()

# Period rate = total deaths / total population over all tracts and all three years.
# Deaths are exact CDC counts where reported, otherwise estimated from the rate (see above).
od_puma_pooled <- od_tract_year %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(deaths), tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    overdose_deaths_2022_2024 = sum(deaths),        # total deaths over 3 years
    overdose_pop_years        = sum(tot_pop),       # person-years at risk
    overdose_rate_2022_2024   = 1e5 * overdose_deaths_2022_2024 / overdose_pop_years,
    n_tract_years             = n(),
    # % of the PUMA's deaths that are estimated from a rate rather than an exact count
    # (left empty for PUMAs with no deaths, where a share can't be calculated)
    pct_deaths_estimated      = if_else(sum(deaths) > 0,
                                        100 * sum(deaths * count_imputed) / sum(deaths),
                                        NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  left_join(od_puma_annual, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  left_join(puma_pop_2020, by = "GEOID20") %>%
  mutate(
    # Coverage: % of the PUMA's person-years with usable data
    pct_popyears_with_overdose_data = 100 * overdose_pop_years / (n_years * puma_pop_2020)
  ) %>%
  select(-puma_pop_2020)

od_puma_pooled %>%
  select(overdose_rate_2022_2024, pct_popyears_with_overdose_data, pct_deaths_estimated) %>%
  summary()

puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  left_join(od_puma_pooled, by = "GEOID20")

puma_final %>%
  filter(is.na(overdose_rate_2022_2024)) %>%
  nrow()                                       # PUMAs with no overdose data at all
```

### Tract-level outcome

```{r}
#| label: cdc-tract-save
# Tract-level overdose outcome, for the tract-level sensitivity check.
# Tracts in the same CDC group share the group's rate, so their tract rates
# aren't independent. A tract-level model should cluster standard errors by group_id!!!

# Tract x year (long format)
od_tract_year %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20)) %>%
  select(GEOID, GEOID20, group_id, year, count_raw, count_imputed, rate, tot_pop, deaths) %>%
  write_csv("data/final/tract_overdose_by_year_2022_2024.csv")

# Pooled 2022-2024 rate per tract
od_tract_year %>%
  filter(!is.na(GEOID20), !is.na(deaths), tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID, GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    overdose_deaths_2022_2024 = sum(deaths),
    overdose_pop_years        = sum(tot_pop),
    overdose_rate_2022_2024   = 1e5 * overdose_deaths_2022_2024 / overdose_pop_years,
    n_years                   = n(),
    pct_deaths_estimated      = if_else(sum(deaths) > 0,
                                        100 * sum(deaths[count_imputed]) / sum(deaths),
                                        NA_real_),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  write_csv("data/final/tract_overdose_2022_2024.csv")
```

## Rurality (RUCA codes)

Share of each PUMA's 2020 population living in each type of RUCA tract.

```{r}
#| label: ruca
ruca <- ruca_raw %>%
  transmute(GEOID = TractFIPS20, ruca = as.numeric(PrimaryRUCA))

# sum(tot_pop * (condition)) adds up the population of the tracts where the condition is TRUE
puma_rural_ruca <- tract_pop_2020 %>%
  select(GEOID, tot_pop) %>%
  inner_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%    # keeps only tracts that have a PUMA
  inner_join(ruca,  by = "GEOID") %>%    # keeps only tracts that have a RUCA code
  filter(!is.na(ruca), ruca != 99, tot_pop > 0) %>%   # 99 = no code (e.g. water-only tracts)
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(
    pct_pop_metro      = 100 * sum(tot_pop * (ruca %in% 1:3)) / sum(tot_pop),   # metropolitan
    pct_pop_micro      = 100 * sum(tot_pop * (ruca %in% 4:6)) / sum(tot_pop),   # micropolitan
    pct_pop_small_town = 100 * sum(tot_pop * (ruca %in% 7:9)) / sum(tot_pop),   # small town
    pct_pop_rural      = 100 * sum(tot_pop * (ruca == 10))    / sum(tot_pop)    # rural
  )

puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  left_join(puma_rural_ruca, by = "GEOID20")

puma_final %>%
  filter(is.na(pct_pop_rural)) %>%
  nrow()                                 # ideally 0
```

## Religion

```{r}
#| label: religion
#| label: religion
# 2020 U.S. Religion Census (county level). *RATE_2020 = adherents as a % of the 2020
# county population, overall and by religious family. Counts people affiliated with a
# congregation, counted where the congregation is (so a few small counties exceed 100%).
# County to PUMA: each tract gets its county's rate; the PUMA value is the
# population-weighted average over its tracts.
religion_county <- readxl::read_excel("data/raw/religion.xlsx") %>%
  transmute(
    county_fips          = sprintf("%05d", as.integer(FIPS)),
    pct_religious        = TOTRATE_2020,
    pct_evangelical      = EVANRATE_2020,
    pct_catholic         = CATHRATE_2020,
    pct_mainline         = MPRTRATE_2020,
    pct_black_protestant = BPRTRATE_2020
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(starts_with("pct_"), ~ pmin(replace_na(.x, 0), 100)))   # missing = no congregations; cap at 100

nrow(religion_county)   # 3,143 counties

puma_relig <- tract_pop_2020 %>%
  inner_join(rel20, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(county_fips = str_sub(GEOID, 1, 5)) %>%
  inner_join(religion_county, by = "county_fips") %>%
  filter(tot_pop > 0) %>%
  group_by(GEOID20) %>%
  summarise(across(starts_with("pct_"), ~ weighted.mean(.x, tot_pop)))

nrow(puma_relig)   # should be 2,462
summary(puma_relig)

puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  select(-any_of(names(puma_relig)[-1])) %>%      # drop old versions if re-running
  left_join(puma_relig, by = "GEOID20")
```

## Analysis dataset

```{r}
#| label: puma-df
# Add columns, area and density, then drop the geometry for the CSV version.
puma_final <- puma_final %>%
  mutate(
    pct_pop_nonmetro = 100 - pct_pop_metro,   # defines the rural subsample (> 50)
    state_fips       = substr(GEOID20, 1, 2), # for state fixed effects / clustering
    land_area_km2    = as.numeric(ALAND20) / 1e6,
    pop_density      = total_pop / land_area_km2,
    log_pop_density  = log(pop_density)
  )

puma_df <- puma_final %>% st_drop_geometry()

nrow(puma_df)                                   # should be 2462
sum(is.na(puma_df$overdose_rate_2022_2024))
sum(is.na(puma_df$pct_divorced_past_yr))
```

## Rural subset and save

Rural PUMAs: more than 50% of the population lives in non-metro (RUCA
4–10) tracts.

```{r}
#| label: rural-subset
# Rural PUMAs: more than 50% of the population lives in non-metro (RUCA 4-10) tracts.
puma_rural <- puma_df %>% filter(pct_pop_nonmetro > 50)
nrow(puma_rural)
```

```{r}
#| label: save
write_csv(puma_df,    "data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.csv")
write_csv(puma_rural, "data/final/rural_puma_dataset_2022_2024.csv")

# With boundaries, for maps and spatial models (delete_dsn overwrites an existing file)
st_write(puma_final, "data/final/national_puma_dataset_2022_2024.gpkg", delete_dsn = TRUE)
```

# Variables {.unnumbered}

| Variable | Meaning | Source |
|----|----|----|
| `GEOID20`, `state_fips` | 7-digit PUMA ID; 2-digit state code | boundary file |
| `total_pop`, `log_pop` | non-institutional population (average year, 2022–2024) and its log | IPUMS |
| `pct_nonwhite`, `pct_nonwhite_nh` | \% not White; % not non-Hispanic White | IPUMS |
| `pct_age_25_54` | \% aged 25–54 | IPUMS |
| `pct_bachelors_plus` | \% of people 25+ with a bachelor's or more | IPUMS |
| `pct_poverty` | \% below the poverty line | IPUMS |
| `pct_unemployed` | \% of the labor force unemployed | IPUMS |
| `medhhinc`, `log_medhhinc` | median household income (2024 \$) and its log | IPUMS |
| `pct_divorced_past_yr` | main divorce outcome: % of ever-married people divorced in the past 12 months, 2022–2024 | IPUMS |
| `pct_divorced_past_yr_2022`, `_2023`, `_2024` | same, single years (noisy, for checks) | IPUMS |
| `pct_divorced_past_yr_atrisk`, `pct_currently_divorced` | alternative divorce measures | IPUMS |
| `n_person_sample`, `n_hh_sample`, `n_divorced_sample` | unweighted sample sizes over 3 years | IPUMS |
| `overdose_rate_2022_2024` | main overdose outcome: deaths per 100,000, 2022–2024 | CDC |
| `overdose_rate_2022`, `_2023`, `_2024` | annual rates (for checks) | CDC |
| `overdose_deaths_2022_2024`, `overdose_pop_years`, `n_tract_years` | deaths, person-years and tract-years behind the period rate | CDC |
| `pct_popyears_with_overdose_data` | \% of the PUMA's person-years with usable data | CDC |
| `pct_deaths_estimated` | \% of the PUMA's deaths estimated from a rate because the count was suppressed | CDC |
| `pct_pop_metro`, `_micro`, `_small_town`, `_rural`, `pct_pop_nonmetro` | \% of population by RUCA tract type | RUCA |
| `land_area_km2`, `pop_density`, `log_pop_density` | land area; people per km²; log | boundary file + IPUMS |
| pct_religious | \% of population who belong to any religion | 2020 U.S. Religion Census |
